analysis.title: Chart of the Day: CCC You Later
key_insights: CCC-rated spreads rose above 1,000 bps for the first time since March 2023 and have widened nearly 450 bps since February. The gap versus BB-rated bonds is the widest since 2020.

Broader high-yield spreads widened 49 bps over the past two weeks to 318 bps amid rate volatility, but remain below the March peak and long-term averages. Investment-grade spreads are near 80 bps with IG yields above 6%. The firm continues to favor higher-quality credit.
Bond volatility is near YTD highs as the global rate selloff intensifies. As of yesterday all major US fixed income sectors were negative YTD, after income offset rising yields for much of the year.
France's 10-year yield topped 4.9% for the first time since 2002. Its spread versus German bonds reached 129 bps, the widest since 2012.

The 10-year Treasury yield rose above 5.3% by end of September. The S&P 500 slipped only 0.5% for the month, but leadership is narrowing: the Equal Weight index is on track for a 7th straight weekly decline, 43% of constituents are in a bear market, and the average stock is down about 21% from its peak. The firm expects leadership to stay narrow until yields stabilize.
The US dollar is up 3.7% YTD and at its highest since April 2025, a mirror image of yield-driven pressure on gold. The firm calls the rally increasingly stretched.

The dollar has moved with oil prices during the Iran conflict, so a meaningful oil drop could trigger profit-taking. The dollar also prices nearly four Fed hikes over 12 months, while the firm expects only one more hike.

Labor signals are mixed ahead of September payrolls: JOLTS was weaker than expected, initial claims stayed below 200k for a third week, and Challenger job cuts fell 20% YoY to the lowest September level since 2022. The firm describes a low-hire, low-fire market and expects a 70k payroll gain.

macro_indicators.interpretation: The firm's 70k estimate sits below the 90k consensus and is described as consistent with a healthy labor market that lets the Fed keep focusing on inflation.

tension_points.bull_case: The dollar is at an 18-month high, up 3.7% YTD, supported by markets pricing nearly four Fed hikes over 12 months and by its tandem moves with oil during the Iran conflict.
tension_points.bear_case: The firm expects only one more hike, not four, and says a meaningful drop in oil could trigger profit-taking.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A meaningful drop in oil prices, or Fed hike pricing converging toward the firm's one-hike expectation.
